verses: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,
they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.
Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.
Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.
When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.
“Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,
“I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
Once again Jesus went out beside the sea. All the people came to Him, and He taught them there.
As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.
While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples—for there were many who followed Him.
When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”
title: Through the Roof
season_line: After yesterday's healed leper spread the news everywhere, Jesus comes home to Capernaum, and the crowds, and the questions, start pressing in.
big_idea: Jesus came to forgive sinners, not to reward the healthy, so no one is too far gone to carry to Him.
frame: Most of us quietly sort people into those who seem close to God and those who seem far. Jesus doesn't sort that way. He sees the sick, and He came for them, which means He came for us too. Sharing faith starts there: not as people who have it together, but as patients who found the Doctor. From {{Isaiah 53:5-6|Isaiah 53:5–6}} to the cross, the whole story of Scripture points to a God who heals by forgiving. Carry that humility into today, and keep your eyes open for someone you could help bring a little closer to Him.

glance.head: Through the Roof
glance.line: Four friends dig through a roof to lower a paralyzed man to Jesus, who first forgives his sins.

glance.head: Authority to Forgive
glance.line: When the scribes object, Jesus heals the man to prove He has authority to forgive sins.

glance.head: Follow Me
glance.line: Jesus calls Levi, a tax collector, and Levi leaves his booth to follow Him.

glance.head: A Doctor for the Sick
glance.line: Jesus eats with tax collectors and sinners, saying He came to call sinners, not the righteous.

understand: Yesterday the cleansed leper told everyone, and Jesus could no longer enter towns openly ({{Mark 1:45|Mark 1:45}}). Now He's back home in Capernaum, likely at Peter's house ({{Mark 1:29|Mark 1:29}}), and the place is packed. Roofs there were flat, made of beams, branches, and packed clay, with stairs outside. So four determined friends climbed up and dug a hole. Jesus saw their faith, the faith of the friends who carried him.

Jesus surprises everyone by speaking to the man's sin before his legs. The scribes are right about one thing: only God forgives sins ({{Isaiah 43:25|Isaiah 43:25}}). So either Jesus is blaspheming, or He is far more than a healer. He calls Himself the Son of Man, a title from {{Daniel 7:13-14|Daniel 7:13–14}}, where one like a son of man receives authority from God Himself. The visible healing proves the invisible forgiveness. This is the first of five conflict stories in Mark (2:1 to 3:6), and that charge of blasphemy will come back at His trial ({{Mark 14:61-64|Mark 14:61–64}}).

Tax collectors worked for the ruling powers, often padded their take, and were seen as traitors. Jesus calls Levi exactly the way He called the fishermen ({{Mark 1:16-20|Mark 1:16–20}}), and Levi throws a dinner for his friends. Sharing a meal back then meant welcome and acceptance, which is why the Pharisees were scandalized. Jesus' answer is simple: doctors go where the sick are. The only people He can't help are those who insist they're fine.

word.gloss: A Greek verb meaning to release, send away, or let go, as in canceling a debt. When Jesus forgives, the sin is not just overlooked; it is sent away from us.

glow: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners

god.short: Name one specific sin to God and hear Jesus' words over it.
god.full: Bring one real, specific sin to God this morning. Then read verse 5 slowly, as if Jesus were saying it to you: Son (or daughter), your sins are forgiven.
god.why: He is faithful to forgive when we confess ({{1 John 1:9|1 John 1:9}}).

together.short: Each name one person you'd love to carry to Jesus; pray one line for them.
together.full: Before you leave, each of you say the name of one person you wish knew Jesus. Pray one sentence for both of them together.

others.short: Reach out to someone outside your usual church circle this week.
others.full: Think of a coworker, neighbor, or old friend who keeps their distance from church people. Send a text today suggesting coffee or lunch, with no agenda but friendship.
others.why: Jesus was known for welcoming and eating with outsiders ({{Luke 15:1-2|Luke 15:1–2}}).

tonight: Who in our life feels like a 'tax collector' to us, someone we'd rather keep at arm's length, and what would sharing a table with them look like?
